chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan narrated to me from his father, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām.
He said: I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, “Does madhy invalidate wudu (ablution)?” He said, “No, and neither the garment nor the body is washed because of it. It is only like saliva and mucus.”

key_terms.الثَّوْبُ: the garment or clothing affected by a substance
key_terms.الْبُزَاقِ: saliva, used as a comparison for legal status
key_terms.الْجَسَدُ: the body in the context of ritual cleanliness
key_terms.الْمَذْيُ: pre-seminal fluid discussed here in relation to ritual purity
key_terms.الْمُخَاطِ: mucus, also used as a comparison for legal status
key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), the minor ritual purification before acts such as salat (prayer)
key_terms.يَنْقُضُ: invalidates or breaks a state of ritual purity
key_terms.يُغْسَلُ: is washed; here referring to whether washing is required

ai.seo_question: Does madhy invalidate wudu (ablution) or require washing the clothes and body?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on madhy, stating that it does not invalidate wudu (ablution). It also clarifies that it is not necessary to wash the body or garment from it, as it is treated like saliva and mucus in ritual purity.
